result:
Solutions 1 and 2 give the same answer, $p^n+p-1$, and their structural claim is plausible: the three subgroups are the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ (order $p^{n-1}$), the $p'$-part (order $p-1$), and the full group (order $p^{n-1}(p-1)$). Their arithmetic checks: $(p-1)+p^{n-1}+p^{n-1}(p-1)=p^{n-1}\cdot p+(p-1)=p^n+p-1$.

Solution 3 rests on an unsupported claim that the qualifying subgroups have index 1, 2, or $p$. Its index-2 subgroup has no justification, and its sum $\frac{p^{n-2}(p-1)(3p+2)}{2}$ is not an integer for every odd $p$ and $n\ge 2$ in general, since the $p^{n-2}(p-1)$ factor is odd only in special cases. I could not verify the classification independently from memory of the literature, so the choice rests on the structural plausibility of Solutions 1 and 2, not on a full proof.

CHOICE: 1
